notes: Libretto by Lorenzo Da Ponte (1790). Words follow the Peters engraving's spelling and punctuation: o ti so pentir (the libretto has fo; the IPA follows the print, the meaning is the libretto's “I'll make you sorry”), Mi da without its accent, c'e in two of the three non c'è più, quì, di grazia pieni (the libretto has grazie), and dell' enorme, dell' uso and quell' aspetto as two words. Peters gives Don Alfonso se costei non ci ravvisa, where the libretto has li (them), so he too says “us”. Ferrando sings with Guglielmo throughout, and Despina joins them in Ah madame and Deh calmate; each singer has their own phrases. Don Alfonso's miei and lei in bars 7 and 9 are sung in two syllables, and their IPA follows the score. IPA, word meanings and translations come from the app's reviewed Così libretto drafts (L27, IPA checked against Castel). IPA follows sung Italian conventions: stressed syllable marked, elisions (two words on one note in the score) joined with ‿, open e/o as ɛ/ɔ. Translation literal, for meaning.
